prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Create a focused visual proposal for a tactical pixel-art game by editing the FIRST reference image (the existing 6 by 6 isometric grass board with three identical shield-bearing soldiers). SECOND reference is a close-up of the exact current grass tile for color/shape matching. Change ONLY the terrain painting. Preserve the complete composition, all three soldiers without redesign, their size/pose/positions, board grid dimensions, tile diamonds with top width:height 4:3 (NOT conventional 2:1), camera angle, thin earth sides, dark background, original title/subtitle/footer typography and spacing. This is a small cleanup of the approved style, not a new biome. Specific improvements: 1) Reduce the conspicuous continuous pale double rims inside the field to a single much quieter low-contrast seam, still readable for tactical cell counting; do not remove the grid. Keep a clear thin outside silhouette. No dark cracks. 2) Replace wiry outlined repeated grass icons with a few compact filled pixel clusters, blades joined at their bases, 2 or 3 broad olive-green light/shadow masses, without striped outlines or tiny scattered bright pixels. Maintain the existing sparse density and plenty of empty flat ground. 3) Vary the few grass-cluster placements and silhouette in a restrained repeating vocabulary so the same large tuft is not stamped at the same front corner on every tile. Leave cell centers clear, never hide soldiers' feet. Keep terrain flatter and lower in contrast than figures. Retain muted moss/olive and brown palette sampled visually from the source, same overall brightness and atmosphere, do not brighten/saturate to lush emerald. Crisp coherent pixel-art shapes, intentional stepped edges at game viewing size, no blur, soft-focus, painterly gradients, random texture, dither, pebbles, cracks, flowers, additional objects, or decorations. The goal is less repetitive texture and less prominent seams, with the exact existing calm tactical scene still recognizable.
